title: The Living Body
subtitle: Tap any colored word to explore it — red for Ayurveda, amber for physiology, olive for anatomy.

blocks.name: Chemical
blocks.info: This stage encompasses atoms and molecules, the tiny particles that are the fundamental components of all living organisms. A collection of atoms and molecules organizes to form a cell.

blocks.name: Cellular
blocks.info: A cell is composed of atoms and molecules and serves as the fundamental unit of life. Many cells join to form a tissue.

blocks.name: Tissue
blocks.info: A tissue consists of a collection of similar cells that collaborate to perform one or more specialized functions. Many tissues join to form an organ.

blocks.name: Organ
blocks.info: An organ is a distinct, structured assembly of tissues that function together to perform specific roles within the body. A collection of organs join to form a system.

blocks.name: System
blocks.info: A system is a collection of interconnected and interdependent organs that collaborate to achieve a particular function or set of functions. A collection of all bodily systems make up the human organism.

blocks.name: The Human Organism
blocks.info: The human organism, the highest level of complexity, is an integrated structure comprising cells, tissues, organs, and systems. Each level is functionally interconnected and crucial for health, as any change in one part affects multiple processes or structures.

segments.t: In Āyurvedic philosophy, the concepts of Trayopastambha, Tridanda, and Purushartha constitute an integrated framework that links daily lifestyle choices to the balance of human health and the overarching purpose of life.

The three pillars of daily life: Āhāra, wholesome, tailored nutrition; Nidrā, restorative sleep for tissue repair and mental renewal; and Brahmacharya, conservation of vital and sexual energy for stamina and resilience. These pillars sustain the Tridanda, the three foundations of the living being.

The three foundations of life: Sharira, the physical body of elements; Sattva, the mind, clarity, emotion, perception; and Ātma, the immortal soul that animates both. When the pillars stabilize the foundations, one gains the strength and clarity to pursue the Purushartha, life's four goals.

The four aims of life: Dharma, ethical duty and righteousness, which frames Artha, wealth and material security, within which one enjoys Kama, sensory pleasure, love, beauty, ultimately leading to Moksha, the spiritual liberation.
